Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organisation of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developed countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilise and catalyse an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity. As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilises its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realisation of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022– 2031. As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organisation and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets, and mobilise and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilise investment flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognise the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including: SME Finance Sub-National Finance Digital Finance UNCDF’s organisational setup includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand), with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States. Duties And Responsibilities UNCDF is looking for a Programme Management Specialist to support the Ghana country programme. The Specialist will be in charge of: Programme Development and Implementation Lead the execution of programmes, ensuring alignment with UNDP and UNCDF rules, regulations and priorities. Lead on annual work plans, making sure HR and procurement needs are correctly assessed and executed, risks are updated, and indicators are aligned with Prodoc. Lead weekly team meetings with project teams, ensuring accountability on follow-up actions. Lead on drafting and quality assurance of donors’ narrative reports based on donors’ agreements, UNCDF’s corporate requirements for reporting schedules for both programmes. Provide guidance on Responsible Party selection; i.e. provide quality assurance on due diligence on pre-selected candidates, selection packages and agreements (Responsible Party, Performance Based Payment Agreement, Letter Of Agreement, Supplementary guidelines). Provide quality assurance support and maintain a relationship with Project Management Support Unit (PMSU) and Operations Effectiveness and Assurance Unit Lead on the overall monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) agenda vis a vis of donor and corporate requirements Establish clear performance targets and indicators with partners, consistent with UNCDF's strategic framework and programmes’ objectives. Financial And Resource Management Manage budgets and ensure efficient allocation of resources. Lead financial reporting and compliance with donor reporting arrangements. Support audits and decentralised evaluations. Ensure effective and efficient use of Quantum and Quantum+ in line with the project cycle. Ensure appropriate staffing and consultants' support is in place, in liaison with regional and HQ support. Organise targets and monitor financial delivery for the programmes. Lead and support the management of HR recruitment and procurement processes, including the preparation of TORs, review and selection of candidates. Knowledge and capacity building, sharing, and advocacy Identify capacity building needs and opportunities of the project team’s members and provide coaching, support and mentoring as needed. Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organised and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia. Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application. Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on development and project-related issues. Support the establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for the dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area. Stakeholder engagement Act as a focal point in-country vis a vis of main stakeholders Participate in donors’ and stakeholder meetings when and as needed in consultation with the regional office Manage the relationships with immediate project stakeholders such as donors, government and other technical partners Support the UNDP country office in making sure the UNCDF results and value added are adequately communicated Competencies Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, and have a lasting impact Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate tasks/barriers and take action to achieve greater results Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate the benefits of a diverse workforce and champion inclusivity Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies Business Direction & Strategy: Strategic Thinking Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight. review_candidates.title: Procurement Manager- Lisbon
review_candidates.description: PURPOSE OF THE ROLE The Procurement Manager is responsible for leading the procurement and supply chain activities of DCS Norway, ensuring that equipment, materials and subcontracted services for MV/HV substation EPC projects are sourced at the right cost, quality and time. The role covers the full procure-to-pay cycle, from tender-stage pricing and supplier selection through contract award, expediting, delivery and close-out, across the company's operations in Norway, Finland and Portugal. Working closely with the Bid team, Design Engineering, Project Managers and Finance, the Procurement Manager builds a reliable and competitive supplier and subcontractor base, manages commercial and supply chain risk, and establishes the procurement processes, frameworks and team needed to support DCS Norway's growth. The role is expected to develop into Head of Procurement as the function grows. Note: DCS Norway operates a competence-based resource model. While this job description defines the primary function of the role, individuals are expected to contribute across other engineering and project functions based on their competencies and the needs of the business. This approach supports team flexibility, professional development, and efficient resource utilisation across projects. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Procurement Strategy & Process Develop and implement the procurement strategy, policies and procedures for DCS Norway in line with company and CTS Group requirements. Define category strategies for key spend areas, including power transformers, GIS/AIS switchgear, protection & control systems, cables, steel structures and civil works. Establish and manage framework agreements and long-term partnerships with strategic suppliers. Set up procurement governance, approval limits and documentation in line with the company IMS and delegations of authority. Select, implement and improve procurement systems and tools to increase efficiency and transparency. Sourcing, Tendering & Contract Award Lead RFQ/RFP processes for equipment, materials and subcontracts, from technical and commercial specification to award. Conduct commercial evaluations and negotiations, securing best value in terms of price, quality, delivery and terms. Prepare and agree purchase orders and subcontracts, ensuring appropriate terms on warranties, liquidated damages, payment and liability. Support the Bid team with supplier pricing, lead times and commercial input during tender preparation. Ensure back-to-back alignment between client contract requirements and supplier/subcontractor terms. Supply Chain, Expediting & Logistics Monitor supplier performance, manufacturing progress and delivery schedules, with particular focus on long-lead equipment. Coordinate factory acceptance tests (FAT), inspections and quality documentation with Engineering and Quality teams. Manage logistics, freight, customs and delivery to project sites in Norway and Finland. Identify supply chain risks (lead times, single-source dependencies, market volatility) and implement mitigation plans. Manage supplier claims, non-conformities, back-charges and warranty issues through to resolution. Supplier & Subcontractor Management Build and maintain a qualified supplier and subcontractor base across the Nordic and wider European markets. Carry out supplier prequalification and periodic evaluation, covering quality, HSE, financial stability, ESG and compliance. Ensure suppliers and subcontractors comply with applicable regulations, including Norwegian requirements on pay and working conditions and contractor liability, where relevant. Develop strategic supplier relationships and drive continuous improvement in cost, quality and delivery. Promote responsible sourcing and compliance with anti-bribery, sanctions and supply chain due diligence requirements (e.g. the Norwegian Transparency Act). Team Leadership, Budget & Reporting Build, lead and develop the procurement team as the function grows, including buyers and expediters. Track procurement spend, savings and commitments against project budgets in collaboration with Project Managers and Finance. Report procurement KPIs, risks and supply market trends to the CEO and leadership team. Ensure procurement records, contracts and approvals are complete, auditable and archived in line with the company IMS. Travel to suppliers, factories and project sites as required. Required Qualifications & Competencies Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration or a related field. A professional procurement qualification (e.g. CIPS) is an advantage. Experience Minimum 8 years' experience in procurement or supply chain management, including at least 3 years in a lead or managerial role. Experience procuring electrical equipment and subcontracts for MV/HV substations, power transmission or energy infrastructure projects is highly desirable. Proven experience in an EPC contractor or project-based engineering and construction environment. Track record of negotiating high-value supply and subcontract agreements and frameworks. Experience setting up or developing procurement processes and teams in a growing organisation is a strong advantage. Technical Skills Strong knowledge of the full procure-to-pay cycle, category management and strategic sourcing. Sound understanding of commercial and contractual terms, including Nordic and international contract forms (e.g. NS 8405/NS 8407, NL/NLM, YSE 1998, FIDIC) and Incoterms. Good technical understanding of substation equipment (transformers, switchgear, protection & control, cables). Knowledge of supply chain compliance, including anti-bribery, sanctions, ESG and supplier due diligence requirements. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills; experience with ERP/procurement systems is an advantage. Ability to analyse total cost of ownership, supplier risk and market trends. Interpersonal & Communication Skills Excellent verbal and written communication in English (Portuguese is considered a plus). Must hold the right to work in the EU/EEA and be available for travel to Norway and Finland as required. Strong organizational and multitasking capabilities. Strong negotiation skills, with the ability to secure value while maintaining long-term supplier relationships. Leadership skills, with the ambition and ability to build and grow a procurement function. High level of integrity and commercial awareness. Collaborative approach when working with engineering, project, finance and bid teams. Strategic Performance Metrics (KPIs) Procurement savings achieved against tender budgets. On-time delivery of critical and long-lead equipment against project schedules. Share of spend covered by framework agreements and prequalified suppliers. Supplier performance (quality, delivery, HSE) and number of supplier non-conformities. Procurement process compliance: approvals, documentation and audit findings. HSE Comply with all applicable health, safety, and environmental legislation, regulations, and company procedures. Integrate safety-by-design principles into all engineering and project activities, ensuring that designs and solutions prioritise the safety of personnel, equipment, and the environment. Participate in risk assessments and hazard identification activities relevant to the role. Report safety concerns, incidents, and near-misses in accordance with company HSE procedures. Support the development and maintenance of a positive safety culture within the team and across projects. Ensure compliance with the company Integrated Management System (IMS) covering quality, safety, and environmental standards. Replacement Policy In case of absence of less than one month, the Procurement Manager will be replaced by the Project Manager designated by the COO. For absences exceeding one month, a temporary replacement will be appointed by senior management. Internal or external recruitment may apply, according to DCS Norway replacement policy guideline The replacement person will assume the key responsibilities outlined in this job description to ensure continuity in procurement and supply chain activities. BENEFITS Addition of variable performance based 0-10% (annual) bonus. This will depend on company and personal performance, and is further subject to an annual performance review; A meal allowance of €10,46 per working day, provided via meal card; Private health insurance coverage for the employee; 22 working days of annual leave, in accordance with Portuguese Labour Law; When you are out of Portugal for work, we will offer the nominal Portugal allowance (approximately €89 per day with 50% payment for last travel day), but the company will pay the accommodation and travel costs (which will be reflected in the contract). When you are away and are paid the daily living away allowance, the meal card payment is not payable.

review_candidates.description: Apply now Job no: 596419 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: Florence Level: Consultancy Location: Kenya Categories: Social Policy Contract Duration: 10.3 Months Working arrangement: HomeBased UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a future. How can you make a difference? UNICEF played a pivotal role in supporting the development of Kenya’s National Safety Net Programme (NSNP), with Government and development partners. The NSNP includes four cash transfer schemes, of which three under the Inua Jamii programme: the Cash Transfer for Orphan and Vulnerable Children (CT-OVC), the Old Person Cash Transfer, and the Persons with Severe Disability Cash Transfer.A fourth scheme focuses on food security and economic resilience in arid and semi-arid lands (the Hunger Safety Net Programme, HSNP).Evaluations of these programmes demonstrated substantial positive impacts on poverty reduction and wellbeing.Despite these findings, social protection coverage remains limited in Kenya, as less than 15% of the poorest households are currently supported by Kenya’s NSNP.Moreover, there remain concerns about the adequacy of transfer amounts, especially for the Inua Jamii schemes, for which the nominal value has remained unchanged since 2013.Concurrently, child poverty persists in Kenya. In 2022 an estimated 42.4% of children lived in monetary poverty.The share of children experiencing multidimensional poverty (deprivations in areas such as health, nutrition, education) increased from 45% in 2014 to 55.3% in 2022.In this context, the CT-OVC is of prominent relevance. Starting in 2004, the programme gradually expanded to about 440,000 households across all counties and constituencies by July 2025.Monthly cash amounts gradually increased from initial KSH 500 to the current amount of KSH 2,000.The main impact evaluation of the CT-OVC, conducted between 2007 and 2011, found that the programme significantly reduced poverty in the short term, with sustained impacts in the medium term; child outcomes improved, including schooling outcomes, as well as health outcomes for young children (in the medium-term). After about 20 years since the start of the CT-OVC, UNICEF Innocenti and UNICEF Kenya initiated a new study to investigate the long-term and intergenerational effects of the CT-OVC. The study is part of the broader Transfer Project, a research learning collaborative led by UNICEF, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill. The study focuses on the original beneficiary children, addressing three main research questions: What were the wellbeing trajectories of beneficiary children (infants 0-4 years, and older children 5-17 years) during receipt of the CT-OVC programme and after graduating from it? How did the CT-OVC affect long-term human development outcomes for children in recipient households, as they transitioned to adulthood? How is the CT-OVC associated with the wellbeing of children born in the new households formed by the original child recipients? The Study Will Use Three Qualitative Approaches A Life Histories approach collecting a detailed record of CT-OVC beneficiaries’ life events, during receipt of the programme and after graduating from it. The Qualitative Impact Protocol (QuIP) methodology to assess long-term effects. Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) with programme stakeholders and policy makers. A local firm will be recruited by UNICEF Kenya to implement data collection activities. Another (international) consultant is being recruited to co-lead the study, with focus on the QUIP component and overall editorial oversight. The consultancy under this TOR is focused on the first and third components of the study, Life Histories and KIIs. Life Histories This method will be used to answer the first research question, while also contributing to answering the other questions. It examines the personal experience of individuals by collecting detailed information on key life events. This allows gaining a deeper understanding of the life trajectory of CT-OVC beneficiaries, including the impact of various events and experiences. KIIs These interviews will be conducted with staff who worked closely with participating families (e.g., community representatives, members of the Location OVC Committees, LOC). These informants can shed light on their personal experiences working with selected beneficiaries and share their observations on changes in the wellbeing and the life trajectory of families, contributing insights to all five research questions. Responses from key informants can especially cover the operational aspects of the CT-OVC. The CT-OVC study sample will include 24 Life Histories and 14 KIIs across two counties in Kenya. Objective Of The Consultancy UNICEF Innocenti is seeking to hire a qualitative research consultant based in Kenya , to co-lead the research study described above, particularly analysis and writing from Life Histories (LHs) and Key Informant Interviews (KIIs). The selected consultant will closely collaborate with the consultant in charge of the QuIP study component (QuIP consultant). Major Areas Of Work And Responsibility Inception: Review programme documents and related literature. In collaboration with the QuIP consultant, prepare the inception mission, including observation checklist for field observation in the pre-selected study locations and methodology for the inception workshop (mission of approximately 5 working days). Study design: Co-develop the final study design and protocol, in collaboration with the QuIP consultant. Prepare the guides for LHs and KIIs; review the QuIP guide, as drafted by the QuIP consultant. Coordinate the ethical review process, addressing the Board requests as needed. Training and support in data collection (LH, KIIs): Conduct training of the local data collection team, in collaboration with the QuIP consultant and the local data collection firm. Supervise the data collection for LHs and KIIs, accompanying the field team during the first week of the operation and supervising remotely afterwards; conduct transcription monitoring for quality assurance (with the data collection firm).
